newsitem.title: USA: M.D.C. Holdings charges hurt Q1 net.
newsitem.headline: M.D.C. Holdings charges hurt Q1 net.

text.p: M.D.C. Holdings Inc said Thursday its diluted earnings per share fell to $0.08 during the first quarter of 1997 versus $0.20 during the 1996 quarter in large part because of two extraordinary charges.
The company said operating results for the first three months ended March 31, 1997 were hurt by a non-cash, pre-tax charge of $1.3 million for the impairment of certain homebuilding assets.
And it cited a previously announced extraordinary $2.2 million loss in the 1997 quarter on repurchase of $38 million of its 11-1/8 percent senior notes Due 2003 for $39.5 million.
The homebuilding company said revenues for the 1997 quarter declined slightly to $193.8 million from $199.2 million during the same period last year.
It said operating earnings slippage was primarily due to decreased revenues in the company's financial services segment and from reduced land sales.
On the positive side, the company said operating profits from its homebuilding operations rose 24 percent to $7.5 million for the first quarter of 1997 from $6.0 million last year.

"We achieved strong operating results in the first quarter of 1997 in Southern California and Phoenix as a result of improved home gross margins and our continued expansion efforts in these markets," said Paris Reece, MDC's chief financial officer.

But he cautioned that although the company expects home gross margins for each of the remaining quarters in 1997 to exceed margins of comparable quarters last year, "we currently estimate that such margins may be lower than margins achieved in the first quarter of 1997."
